name: MIRHAL
summary: A bilingual personal-growth platform that turns long-term goals into meaningful daily action.
description: MIRHAL brings goals, milestones, projects, tasks, habits, reflection, and progress into one connected experience. The product includes a customer application, a separate administration experience, and a shared API. Arabic and English, RTL/LTR layouts, themes, responsive navigation, and installable PWA support are part of the product design.
imageAlt: MIRHAL product identity and platform preview.
previewNote: The existing live link is an earlier release; the current repository documents newer work that has not yet been deployed. The admin portal requires an authorized staff account.
highlights: Goals, milestones, projects, tasks, and subtasks
Habit schedules, streaks, and habit experiments
Quests, XP, achievements, and personal rewards
Arabic/English localization with full RTL/LTR support
Separate customer and staff administration applications
Session-based authentication and privacy-conscious offline caching

name: Ehsebha
summary: An Arabic-first operating system that helps ride-share and delivery drivers understand their real profit.
description: Ehsebha is designed for drivers whose earnings are spread across trips, fuel, commissions, expenses, and vehicle maintenance. The product combines trip and expense management, profitability analytics, OCR-assisted receipt extraction, and planning tools in a bilingual PWA. Its repository separates the React web experience from the NestJS API and PostgreSQL data layer.
previewNote: The GitHub README documents the current React PWA and NestJS architecture. Verify the deployed demo and authentication availability before presenting it as a fully working production demo.
highlights: Driver earnings, trip, expense, and vehicle-cost tracking
Profitability analytics and what-if planning
Arabic-first RTL interface with English support
OCR-assisted Arabic/English receipt and trip extraction
Installable PWA with offline-tolerant app shell

name: 3D Otaku
summary: An Egypt-focused storefront for 3D-printed products, combining commerce workflows with interactive 3D previews.
description: 3D Otaku explores the engineering behind a specialized product storefront: catalog discovery, product details, 3D visualization, cart and checkout flows, customer accounts, and operational administration. The frontend uses Angular 21, SSR, Three.js, Tailwind CSS 4, and PrimeNG. The repository also documents a separate Express/MongoDB backend and detailed deployment, asset-integrity, and operational verification work.
imageAlt: 3D Otaku product storefront and interactive 3D product preview.
previewNote: The source repository is private. The public demo is available at the link below; source-code access is not publicly available.
highlights: 3D product viewer with WebGL context-loss and recovery handling
Product catalog and responsive storefront experiences
Cart, checkout, customer account, and admin workflows
SSR and server-side API integration
Asset integrity, performance, and browser QA tooling

name: Online Exam
summary: A structured online examination experience built with Angular 21 and reusable authentication integration.
description: Online Exam is an Angular application organized around a clear examination workflow. The repository uses Angular 21, TypeScript, PrimeNG, Tailwind CSS 4, RxJS, and a reusable authentication library. Its current README is framework-generated, so detailed claims about exam lifecycle, timer behavior, grading, and backend integration should be confirmed against the application screens and source before publication.
imageAlt: Online Exam Angular application sign-in screen.
previewNote: The repository is public. The README contains Angular CLI setup information rather than a complete product specification; this case study intentionally limits claims to verified stack and project identity.
highlights: Angular 21 application structure
Reusable authentication package integration
PrimeNG and Tailwind-based UI stack
Vitest-based testing setup

name: Sakny · سكني
summary: An Arabic-first shared-apartment app that brings rent, shared expenses, contributions, and household responsibilities into one transparent workspace.
description: Sakny helps residents manage the practical and financial side of living together in Egypt. It distinguishes expenses paid from the apartment contribution pool from expenses split among members, keeps an auditable record, and rotates household responsibilities. The resident app and separate administrator experience use Angular 22, strict TypeScript, Firebase Authentication and Firestore, with an authenticated server API for sensitive operations.
imageAlt: Sakny shared apartment management platform preview.
previewNote: The source repository is private. The live resident app is public; the administrator portal requires authorized access.
highlights: Arabic-first bilingual shared-apartment management
Separate shared-pool contributions and member-split expenses
Server-side transactional financial writes and auditable history
Rotating household responsibilities and task notifications
Independent platform administration and support workflows
Browser QA covering responsive layouts and Arabic/English direction

name: Postify
summary: A focused content experience exploring searchable posts, discussions, and form feedback.
description: Postify is a small Angular application built around a posts API. It demonstrates signal-based filtering, post details, comments, validated forms, loading states, and user feedback. The project uses JSONPlaceholder for demonstration, so created posts and comments are simulated rather than persistently stored.
previewNote: Demo uses JSONPlaceholder; write operations are simulated and are not persisted.
highlights: Signal-based search and filtering
Post details and comments
Validated post/comment form UI
Loading, empty, and error feedback states
